https://enrsi.stvr.sk/articles/topical-i.text: Peter Stano, Head of the European Commission Representation in Slovakia says that the European Commission is monitoring Slovakia’s national park zoning reform while assessing the country’s eighth payment request under the Recovery and Resilience Plan. The dispute centres on the transfer of forest management from the state forestry company to national parks, with up to 450 million euros in EU funding potentially at stake. State Secretary Filip Kuffa claims the Commission shares his concerns that government amendments have weakened the reform, while Environment Minister Tomáš Taraba rejects those claims, insisting the zoning fully complies with EU requirements. The government has signed a memorandum between the environment and agriculture ministries to clarify the transfer of land management, but opposition parties and environmental organisations argue the document is not legally binding and are calling for the disputed government resolutions to be amended or withdrawn. Source: TASR, STVR

A spokesman for Germany's Foreign Ministry in Berlin announced that the agenda for the meeting, held in the so-called Weimar Triangle format, covers topics ranging from hybrid threats and the situation in the Middle East, to EU enlargement and a reform of EU foreign policy. Hybrid threats are understood to mean a combination of military, economic, intelligence and propaganda measures, which can be used to influence public opinion. State-sponsored cyberattacks are included in this category. In Ireland, the focus was on reactions to the German government's attribution of responsibility to Russia for the attempted attack on August 4 at Leipzig airport. The Weimar Triangle was established in 1991 as a forum for dialogue by the then foreign ministers of the three countries in the central German city of Weimar. Initially, its primary purpose was to facilitate the integration of Poland and other Eastern European states into the European Union and NATO.
